item.title: No. 11 Texas rolls past Mississippi State for rare stress-free win of late
item.description: Texas defensive lineman Maraad Watson (88) celebrates his fumble return TD with defensive coordinator Will Muschamp and teammates during the Longhorns' win over Mississippi State on Saturday in Austin. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) AUSTIN - Arch Manning threw for three touchdowns, and 11th-ranked Texas added a defensive score to finally win without any drama as the Longhorns overwhelmed Mississippi State 31-3 on Saturday night at Royal-Memorial Stadium. Heck, they even scored a touchdown in the third quarter. The Longhorns' second straight victory was anything but a showcase, however. Texas failed to show any kind of ground game, rushing for just 60 yards and giving up five sacks to a Bulldogs defense that ranked 14th in the SEC. Playing without injured All-Americans at edge rusher (Colin Simmons) and left tackle (Trevor Goosby), Texas produced a workmanlike effort to thwart the punchless Bulldogs and almost pitched a shutout. Mississippi State's lone score came of Kyle Ferrie's 30-yard field goal midway through the second quarter. The Longhorns improved to 6-2 with their second consecutive home win and 3-2 in league play before preparing to embark on the stretch drive with three of their last four games on the road. Texas goes to Missouri next week for an 11 a.m. kickoff. Mississippi State, which lost its spectacular quarterback Kamario Taylor to toe surgery, was never a threat and fell to 4-4 and 2-4 in SEC action. Manning threw for at least three touchdowns for the third time this season and the eighth time in his career. He completed 16 of 20 passes for 220 yards with one fumble and ran 13 times for a net 10 yards. The Bulldogs put up a good fight for a while with two electric offensive players in Anthony Evans III, the SEC's leading receiver, and physical running back Fluff Bothwell, the fourth-leading rusher in the conference. Texas finally got another defensive touchdown - its second of the season - to compensate for yet another sluggish offensive performance. Defensive lineman Maraad Watson's scoop and score after a fumble forced by linebacker Rasheem Biles' sack went for 61 yards and completely shifted the momentum of the game. Trailing just 10-0 late in the second quarter, the Bulldogs had just pinned the Longhorns inside their 10 and gotten terrific field position at the Texas 46. Four plays later, Biles came on a delayed blitz and sacked surprise starter AJ Swann, causing the fumble and injuring the third-string quarterback's shoulder. Watson, a 6-3, 333-pound defensive tackle, gathered in the ball like an all-star shortstop and sprinted up the right sideline with a convoy of blockers. It marked the first defensive score since the season opener against Texas State when nickel back Graceson Littleton ran back a fumble recovery 59 yards for a touchdown. item.title: Army football struggles on road in soggy loss to Memphis
item.description: Army football tasted defeat for the first time in nearly a month, and now the Black Knights ' focus must shift toward their most important goal of the season: contending for the Commander-in-Chief's Trophy. The Black Knights struggled to stop Memphis' high-powered offense all night and the Tigers kept alive their American Conference title-game hopes with a 49-22 victory at Liberty Stadium on Saturday, October 31. Army last tasted defeat on Oct. 3, 31-29 at Louisiana Tech. The loss likely takes Army (5-3, 4-2 American) out of the title chase in their third season as a member — the Black Knights won in their inaugural season in 2024. Memphis produced seven touchdowns, punting three times and fumbling once. The Tigers rolled up 554 yards of offense, with quarterback Marcus Stokes passing for 371. Once staked to a big lead late, the Tigers primarily kept the ball on the ground to eat clock, rolling up 183 rushing yards. "They kicked our butts today," Army head coach Jeff Monken said. "They flat beat us.'' Army's offense struggled in the first half, leading to three James Wagenseller punts, while Memphis converted four of its five drives into touchdowns — a forced fumble by Noah Nixon off a Memphis reception and recovery by Kody Harris-Miller was the Tigers' only failure. Stokes delivered as advertised, and more. Running an up-tempo offense with hardly a huddle, Stokes was 20-for-23 passing for 258 yards in the first half. Memphis went 12 plays on 80 yards, five plays for 75, turned the ball over on the reception and fumble, and then went eight plays for 68 and 12 plays for 86 on its four touchdown drives. Stokes used five different receivers for six grabs and 55 yards on the Tigers' opening series. Stokes found Jermane Hayes in the left corner of the end zone and the receiver tapped down both feet on the edge for the 13-yard score. Army responded nicely, using eight run plays to go 75 yards as Godspower Nwawuihe went off a heavy presence on the left side from 5 yards out. Stokes floated a 51-yard pass to Hunter Tipton to ignite the second series. Three receptions later, it was Hayes again, using two picks by his receivers on the right side to snare a 5-yard pass across the front of the end zone for a 14-7 lead. Army punted but got the ball back on Harris-Miller's fumble recovery at the Memphis 13. Hellums directed a four-play, game-tying drive; a short shovel pass to Samari Howard turning into an 8-yard score. Again, Stokes completed four passes on his next series. A 16-yard leaping grab by Hunter Tipton set up a 1-yard dive off the left side by Jaylin Carter. Army football: Soggy second half The rain forecast proved accurate, starting with a light rain to start the third quarter and then turning into a steady downpour as the second half progressed. Army scored on its second series after the break and then had to punt twice. The last two series ended with interceptions, one thrown by Cale Hellums, the last by backup Bryson Luter to end the game. item.description: Texas edge Zina Umeozulu (19) celebrates a sack during the game against Mississippi State at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, 2026 in Austin. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) For the Texas football team, Halloween featured more treats than tricks. Led by its defense, UT never trailed during Saturday night's 31-3 win over Mississippi State at Royal-Memorial Stadium. The 11th-ranked Longhorns got three touchdown passes from quarterback Arch Manning, but it was a defense that contributed a score by defensive lineman Maraad Watson and seven sacks that shined the brightest in the 28-point triumph. More: Subscribe to the Statesman's Texas sports newsletter With the victory, Texas improved its record to 6-2 on the season. The Longhorns are 3-2 in SEC play. Coleman turned that third play into a 47-yard gain after he hauled in a hitch in traffic and then scored on a 14-yard touchdown catch. That was the seventh touchdown catch of the season for Coleman, who celebrated the score with the famed dance from Michael Jackson's "Thriller" music video. item.title: South Central runners dominate District 3 cross country meet
item.description: A dozen titles were handed out in six races, but there was one dominant league at the District 3 cross country championships Saturday, Oct. 31. The newly named and expanded South Central Athletic Conference brought home half of the gold medals, three times more than any other conference. Four schools won team titles in the Halloween races on the Big Spring High School course, two girls and two boys. It was the first time since 2020 that the former YAIAA won four team titles. Boys from Dallastown and Big Spring claimed individual titles. An additional team qualified for the PIAA meet, which brings the runners back to Big Spring on Nov. 7, as well as numerous individual runners. The top 20 boys and girls received medals in Class 2A and 3A and the top 10 in Class A. Making history at Shalom Christian It only took the Flames three seasons in the PIAA to win the school's first District 3 title. The boys grouped their five runners from eighth to 17th place in scoring positions to claim the Class A team title. Schools that don't have enough runners to form a team are included in overall positions, but aren't counted in team places. Will Davis finished 10th overall, but two runners ahead of him weren't part of the team competition, so his finish earned him eight points. The Flames finished with 62 points to outdistance Anchor Christian by 30 points. The rest of the Flames points came from Shay Kane (10), Owen Book (12), Matthew Davis (15) and Lee Metcalf (17). "We put in the work, this is what we were working for all season, and we knew we could do it," Davis said. He said the tight grouping was a formula that worked well for them all season, so they weren't going to change it for districts. And now the Flames have a chance to add to their story with a good showing at the PIAA meet. "It's a payout for the hard work we have been putting in over the season," Metcalf said. "Sticking together, team building. Leaving districts as a team in first place, states is going to be our reward run for finishing so well." Back-to-back champs York Catholic coach Jeff Alloway kept refreshing his phone, waiting for the official race results to be posted. He thought his girls had a chance to successfully defend their Class A team title, but he wasn't sure. It was that close with Covenant Christian Academy. "I was very pleased with all six runners," Alloway said. "If one or two of them has a bad day, we don't have a next week." Abby Bullen led the Irish with a personal-best 19:47.7 to finish second behind Covenant Christian's Alex Sagen, who won in 18:56.6. Alloway challenged Bullen to be more aggressive in her third mile, something she took to heart in the district meet. But he admitted it was tough for her to do with no one around her. Bullen was nearly a minute behind Sagen and nearly a minute ahead of Shalom Christian's Kassidy Hubers. item.title: Can Cincinnati Bearcats football win in November?
item.description: October is in the books for the Cincinnati Bearcats with a not-so-pleasing 1-3 record after being routed 49-25 by No. 6 Utah on Halloween night. The Bearcats began with a 4-0 September, never leaving Cincinnati, before beginning October with a late-night lopsided loss in the desert to Arizona and a last-minute heartbreaker in West Virginia. Now it's onto November and a month that hasn't been kind to head coach Scott Satterfield during his UC tenure. The Bearcats will begin at Houston Nov. 7, a team that lost to Utah only 21-13 in Salt Lake City, Oct. 24. "We come in every game expecting to win, and it's frustrating when we don't," UC quarterback JC French IV said. "We're all really frustrated right now with how we played, but I think we can compete with anybody in this conference and country. That's just something we have to hold ourselves to, keep moving forward and bounce back next game." November wins few, far between for Cincinnati Bearcats The last November win for UC under Satterfield came in his opening season of 2023. It was also UC's first Big 12 victory. After a 2-0 start, including a win at Pitt, UC dropped seven straight games until Nov. 11 when they picked off Houston quarterback Donovan Smith three times and Corey Kiner ran for 129 yards and two touchdowns. UC won 24-14 and Cougars coach Dana Holgorsen was fired two weeks later. Nearly three years later, that's UC's only Big 12 November win. UC Bearcats favorable starts have turned into November nightmares The 2024 season was highlighted by beating Arizona State on Homecoming, Oct. 19, 24-14. The Sun Devils and future NFL running back Cam Skattebo would go on a run that put them in the College Football Playoff. UC would proceed to lose at Colorado on Oct. 26, then drop all four games in November to West Virginia, Iowa State , Kansas State and TCU to go from 5-2 to 5-7 with no postseason invites to anything. Last season, many remember the 7-1 start as the Bearcats reeled off seven wins in a row after the opening loss to Nebraska. Then came Nov. 1 at No. 24 Utah, with the pageantry of ESPN College GameDay that morning in Salt Lake City. Later that night, the Utes ran by the Bearcats 45-14, with the first of four November losses. From there, it was a giveaway game vs. Arizona , a missed opportunity at home vs. No. 11 BYU , and Brendan Sorsby's finale at TCU. A flurry of opt-outs followed for the Jan. 2 FedEx Liberty Bowl vs. No. 22 Navy and UC was 0-for-November again, with a fifth straight loss against the Midshipmen, where opting out is highly discouraged. item.title: "Terrible": Deion Sanders’ Son Left Disappointed as Colorado Players and Staff Celebrate Kansas State Upset
item.description: Deion Sanders ©Credits: IMAGO After five straight losses, Colorado finally had a reason to celebrate. But as the Buffaloes secured a 27-24 overtime victory against Kansas State for their first Big 12 win of the season, one voice stood completely apart from the party. The final whistle brought plenty of excitement to Boulder. Colorado players and staff celebrated on the field, while fans in Halloween costumes rushed past the barriers and joined the celebrations. Some even helped bring down the goalposts as the crowd enjoyed a win that had taken weeks to arrive. While the field erupted in full-blown chaos, head coach Deion Sanders’ son, Deion Jr., cut through the celebration with a stark message. “I ain’t even trying to be a part of it, but she was terrible. It’s a terrible showing, guys. There ain’t no reason to celebrate. I’m not trying to be a part of it, but that s–t was terrible. S–t was unacceptable, guys,” Deion Sanders Jr. said while recording himself after the game on 1 November. Credits: IMAGO As the media brain behind ‘Well Off Media’ and Coach Prime’s eldest son, Sanders Jr. is a constant presence inside the locker room, making his blunt critique far more than just standard fan chatter. Shedeur Sanders expected a different outcome in Boulder. Subscribe to stay updated on Colorado football's pivotal moments and the pressure mounting on Deion's program. Sanders Jr.’s comments stood out as Colorado was still celebrating its overtime victory. He repeated that the showing was terrible and questioned why there was a reason to celebrate. However, the video does not clearly establish what he was referring to, so his remarks cannot be directly linked to the players and staff celebrating on the field. The comments also bring back an earlier moment involving his father and Kansas State. In October 2024, Deion Sanders publicly addressed his son Shilo Sanders’ performance after Colorado suffered a 31-28 loss to the Wildcats. That was a separate incident, but it adds some context to the attention surrounding the Sanders family following another Kansas State matchup. For Colorado, Saturday’s result was a welcome change after a difficult few weeks. The Buffaloes entered the game with a 2-5 record and had not won a Big 12 game since October 11, 2025. Another defeat would have made an already challenging season even harder, but the team found a way to come through when it mattered. The Buffaloes did not get the win without a fight. They looked close to finishing the game in regulation, but Kansas State scored a touchdown with just two seconds left to make it 21-21. That sent the game into overtime and gave both teams another chance to take control. Kansas State got the ball first in the extra period but had to settle for a field goal, putting the Wildcats ahead 24-21. Colorado needed a touchdown to finish the game, and quarterback Isaac Wilson delivered. He connected with tight end Charlie Williams for an 11-yard score, giving the Buffaloes the 27-24 win

item.description: (Photo by Eston Parker/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) | ISI Photos via Getty Images Wow. All I can immediately muster as I sit down at my computer. The Miami Hurricanes remained perfect on Saturday night in Chapel Hill, just barely getting past North Carolina 38-35. Darian Mensah was 22/29 passing for 274 yards and three scores with no interceptions. Mark Fletcher, Jr. had 13 rushes for 43 yards with two touchdowns and added a 31-yard receiving touchdown. Malachi Toney had seven catches for 75 yards and two touchdowns. Chase Smith, JJ Dunnigan, and Mohamed Toure all led Miami with 9 total tackles each. As the score indicates, it was a defense optional contest from the start. Miami went 74 yards in 13 plays to take a 7-0 lead. Mensah lobbed a ball towards the sideline in the end zone to Toney, who made an incredible blind catch over the shoulder that I can’t do justice with words for a two-yard score. UNC punted (I don’t write those words again in this piece, very sadly), on the ensuing drive, but Miami punted it back six plays later. And that’s when Miami’s 2024 defense trotted out onto the field. The Hurricanes were an absolute disaster as a unit, missing tackle after tackle, particularly on the perimeter, and getting absolutely eaten alive in zone coverage. Carolina went off in the second quarter, putting together an 11-play, 84-yard drive and a 12-play, 75- yard drive, both of which ended in touchdown passes to UNC TE Jelani Thurman, who Miami made look like the greatest college tight end I’ve ever seen. The Hurricanes had their own touchdown in between, with Mark Fletcher, Jr. lining up wide in the back side of a diamond formation near the sideline. He took a quick pass from Mensah, and the trio in front of him forged a lane that he took 31 yards to the house. The Hurricanes added a field goal shortly before the halftime whistle for a 17-14 lead. item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect MONTREAL — The Pittsburgh Penguins are not good in the defensive zone. And 14 games into the season, they have shown they’re equally inept at puck management. Even coach Dan Muse admitted he sounds like a broken record, but the Penguins again made bewildering mistakes in the defensive zone, and turnovers cost them yet another game. The Penguins smoked their own meats against the Montreal Canadiens, before a furious third-period comeback fell short. The Penguins deservedly lost to Montreal 5-4 at Bell Center. However, the comeback wasn’t much of a salve for the Penguins. Captain Sidney Crosby , who had a goal and two assists, essentially dismissed it as too little, too late against an opponent who eased up. “I think just when you’re down, obviously you get a little more aggressive, and sometimes it’s a little bit of us being aggressive and then maybe (them) sitting back a little bit,” said Crosby. “So, within two, there’s still a lot of hockey left in the game, and I thought we pushed pretty well, and just couldn’t find a way to tie it up.” The Penguins’ breakdowns were once again ruinous, and rookie goalie Sergei Murashov battled his game as much as he battled the puck, allowing a couple of soft goals in addition to the team’s defensive coverage leaving him fully exposed on a few more. Montreal twice scored two quick goals, 27 and 24 seconds apart, respectively. And they scored several goals on chances NHL teams don’t get but once every few weeks. For the Penguins, they gift can’t-miss chances several times per period. “I know it sounds like a broken record, but we didn’t play consistently,” Muse said. “I think tonight–hockey is a game of mistakes, so mistakes are going to happen–but you can’t let (them) be able to get two quick ones, or even sometimes just shifts where they’re getting multiple chances back to back. We need to be better at just controlling momentum. And tonight, I thought that factored in.” Murashov was not sharp Saturday. He put himself and the team in a first-period hole, but the team did little to help. item.title: The 2026 CFB season was always going to be about Notre Dame VS Miami
item.description: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - AUGUST 31: CJ Carr #13 of the Notre Dame Fighting Irish looks to pass against the Miami Hurricanes during the second quarter of the game at Hard Rock Stadium on August 31, 2025 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Megan Briggs/Getty Images) | Getty Images I’m almost completely certain Notre Dame will drop from No. 5 in the AP Top 25 this week to No.7 when the rankings are released Sunday afternoon. I’m also certain that Notre Dame will be No. 7 or No. 8 in the initial College Football Playoff rankings. And that’s fine, and it likely doesn’t matter much. I just watched Miami escape with a win for the second week in a row (with some help from the officials) but they WILL be No. 1 when they come up to South Bend next weekend with ESPN’s College Gameday in attendance. Despite Notre Dame’s one loss this season, the game in South Bend is going to be a monster. Some might argue that a No. 1 Notre Dame and No. 2 Miami facing off would be a whole lot bigger (which is what it would be had the Irish pulled off a win against BYU) but that’s just window dressing. An undefeated Miami and undefeated Notre Dame would basically only be playing for playoff seeding and not for their playoff lives — and the latter is exactly what Notre Dame is fighting for on Saturday. It means more, but we knew this was THE game in 2026 ever since the Irish lost to Miami to start the 2025 season. It’s been going on for weeks, but the debate about if a two loss Notre Dame team can make the playoffs is going strong. Regardless of my own personal thoughts, and the fact CFB as a whole has been completely chaotic this season, I refuse to engage with those debates. Beat Miami. Beat Miami, and run the table and nothing else matters. The other results don’t matter and some random dude’s opinion doesn’t matter. Beat Miami and the Irish are going to be in the CFB playoff. This season was always going to be about this game. The different type of stakes have changed, but the spotlight is on and it’s as bright as the sun. Beat Miami and this Notre Dame team will make a run. Beat Miami.

item.title: Ohio State’s Season Comes Crashing Down as USC Pulls Off Massive Upset
item.description: Photo by: Adam Cairns The USC Trojans pulled off one of the biggest upsets of the college football season Saturday night, knocking off the No. 2 Ohio State Buckeyes 30-18 at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. Head coach Lincoln Riley and his Trojans delivered a statement performance, handing Ohio State its second loss of the season and shaking up the Big Ten championship picture. Ohio State entered the matchup as one of the nation’s top teams, but head coach Ryan Day faced an additional challenge with starting quarterback Julian Sayin unavailable because of a throwing-arm injury. Freshman Luke Fahey received the starting opportunity against a USC team desperate for a bounce-back performance. USC Comes Out Firing The Trojans wasted no time getting their offense going. Quarterback Jayden Maiava connected with wide receiver Trent Mosley for a spectacular 69 yard touchdown, giving USC an early 7-0 advantage. Ohio State responded with a field goal, but USC continued applying pressure. Running back Waymond Jordan found the end zone on a nine yard touchdown run, extending the lead to 14-3. The Buckeyes struggled to find consistency offensively, settling for another field goal in the second quarter. USC answered with a 54 yard field goal of its own, taking a 17-6 advantage. The Trojans added another field goal before halftime, entering the locker room with a 20-9 lead. Maiava and Riley Deliver Against Ohio State Maiava played an important role in USC’s offensive success, finishing with 222 passing yards and a touchdown. Although the Trojans did not dominate time of possession, they made their opportunities count. Mosley was particularly impressive, finishing with 101 receiving yards and providing the explosive plays USC needed. On the other sideline, Fahey faced an enormous challenge in his first start against a nationally elite opponent. He finished with 240 passing yards, but Ohio State struggled to turn its offensive production into points. Running back Bo Jackson provided a bright spot for the Buckeyes, rushing for 121 yards. Ohio State’s Comeback Falls Short Ohio State attempted to make things interesting in the second half, scoring nine fourth quarter points. However, USC’s defense continued making important stops when it mattered most. Riley’s team maintained its composure and refused to allow the Buckeyes to complete the comeback. The Trojans finished with 339 total yards, while Ohio State accumulated 444. Despite the significant difference in yardage, USC’s ability to capitalize on scoring opportunities proved decisive. A Massive Statement for USC The victory gives Riley and USC an enormous confidence boost heading into the remainder of the Big Ten schedule. For Day and Ohio State, the loss raises questions about the quarterback situation with Sayin sidelined and whether the Buckeyes can maintain their championship aspirations. item.title: Barack Obama, Martina Navratilova & Others React After Gabby Williams Makes Valkyries Fastest Expansion Team in American Pro Sports History to Win a Title
item.description: SAN FRANCISCO, CA – OCTOBER 17: Gabby Williams 1 of the Golden State Valkyries celebrates during the last few second of Game One of the WNBA, Basketball Damen, USA Playoff Finals against the Atlanta Dream on October 17, 2026 at Chase Center in San Francisco, CA. Photo by Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire WNBA: OCT 17 Finals Atlanta Dream at Golden State Valkyries EDITORIAL USE ONLY Icon261017028 ©IMAGO/Icon Sportswire At halftime of the first Game 7 in WNBA Finals history, the Golden State Valkyries trailed by six. Their star, Gabby Williams, had two points. A first title for either team was on the line, and Atlanta led. Then everything flipped. Williams scored 28 points in the second half, and the Valkyries won 68-63 at Chase Center in San Francisco. The congratulations came quickly, starting at the very top. Former US President Barack Obama posted on X , “Congrats to the new WNBA champs, the @Valkyries! Ballhalla was rocking all season, and this team was fun to watch. Enjoy the celebration.” Tennis great Martina Navratilova followed with a message for the star of the night: “Gabby Williams rules :), #1 jersey and #1 on the floor, well done.” The Valkyries just rewrote the expansion playbook. Subscribe to stay across the WNBA's most electrifying storylines and the athletes reshaping women's sports. Nike Basketball then posted, “Some rings happen fast. Only two years into their existence as a franchise, the Golden State Valkyries are the 2026 WNBA Champions.” The NBA wrote, “IN JUST THEIR 2ND SEASON, GOLDEN STATE ARE WNBA CHAMPIONS. Congratulations @valkyries.” That win made Golden State the WNBA champion in just its second season. Looking back to 1967, the start of the NFL’s Super Bowl era, no expansion team in the NBA, WNBA, NHL, MLB, or NFL has won a title faster. The 1970-71 Milwaukee Bucks held the old record. Williams earned the praise she deserved after being named the Finals MVP. She scored 30 points on 10-of-23 shooting, hit four three-pointers and made all six of her free throws, and added four blocks and two steals. Her four blocks tied Veronica Burton and Diana Taurasi for the most by a guard in a Finals game. Before Game 7, she was averaging 17.8 points and 2.7 steals in the series. Williams scored the team’s final 11 points of the third quarter, 15 in all for the period, and hit three straight threes to cut Atlanta’s lead to two.
